- Overestimate prices after strong sentiment spikes (especially sentiment > 0.67) — reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently low (< 0.33) — adjust upward by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent sentiment shifts — delay peak predictions by 1–3 days if sentiment is trending.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >75% from prior day) — cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), forecast should align with recent 7-day average — avoid long-term extrapolation.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 3 days, adjust future forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day to correct for momentum bias.
- High sentiment + high recent price = overconfidence bias — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment > 0.7 and price > 75.00.
